Order 
The instant Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant-claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation amount by challenging the impugned Award dated 05.11.2022 passed by the Third Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jaura District Morena (in short "the Claims Tribunal") in Motor Accident Claim Case No. 72/2021,
whereby the Claims Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs. 3,35,394/- in favour of the claimant along with interest.

sentences.text: 2. Along with the appeal, the appellant has filed I.A. No. 6865 of 2023, an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act seeking condonation of delay in filing the present appeal.
As per the office report, there is a delay of 244 days in filing the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7943 2 MA-6205-2023 3.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the impugned award was passed on 05.11.2022 and the statutory period of limitation for filing an appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act is 90 days, which expired on 03.02.2023.
However, the present appeal has been filed on 05.10.2023, resulting in a delay of 244 days.

It is submitted that the delay occurred due to the ailment suffered by the appellant after the accident and due to lack of communication between the Sonu Rawat vs Pradeep Kumar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164033998/
1 appellant and his counsel.
It is further contended that the appellant is a poor and rustic villager who is not conversant with the technicalities of law and, therefore, could not contact his counsel within the prescribed time.

It is further submitted that after a considerable lapse of time, when the counsel informed the appellant in the month of August, 2023 regarding the passing of the award dated 05.11.2022, the appellant immediately contacted the counsel after collecting the necessary papers.
Thereafter, the counsel advised him to prefer an appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.
The appeal was accordingly drafted in the month of September, 2023 and was thereafter filed on 05.10.2023.
It is contended that the delay in filing the appeal is neither intentional nor deliberate but occurred due to bona fide reasons.
Therefore, it is prayed that the delay be condoned in the interest of justice.
4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company has vehemently opposed the application for condonation of delay.
It is submitted that the appellant has failed to furnish any day-to-day explanation for the inordinate delay of 244 days.

According to the Insurance Company,
the pleas that the appellant is a poor and rustic villager and that there was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7943 3 MA-6205-2023 non-communication with counsel are vague and stereotyped excuses which do not constitute "sufficient cause" within the meaning of Section 5 of the Limitation Act.

It is further contended that upon expiry of the limitation period, a valuable right has accrued in favour of the Insurance Company, which should not be lightly disturbed in the absence of a cogent and satisfactory explanation for the delay.

5. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
The law regarding condonation of delay is well-settled.

While a liberal approach is generally adopted in matters arising from the Motor Vehicles Act, being a social welfare legislation, the term "sufficient cause"
cannot be expanded to the extent of rendering the Law of Limitation redundant.

7. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Esha Bhattacharjee v. Managing Committee of Raghunathpur Nafar Academy, (2013) 12 SCC 649, observed that "the concept of liberal approach has to encapsulate the conception of adjudication of disputes on merits and not to enable a party to take the law for granted.

entities.text: Esha Bhattacharjee v. Managing Committee of Raghunathpur Nafar Academy, (2013) 12 SCC 649
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Lack of bona fides imputable to a party seeking condonation of delay is a significant and relevant fact."

Similarly, in the matter of Postmaster General v. Living Media India Ltd., (2012) 3 SCC 563, the Hon'ble Apex Court held that in the absence of a plausible and acceptable explanation, the delay cannot be condoned mechanically.

entities.text: Postmaster General v. Living Media India Ltd., (2012) 3 SCC 563
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. In the present case, the delay in filing the appeal is 244 days, which is considerable.

The explanation offered by the appellant is that he is a poor and rustic villager and that there was non-communication between him and NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:7943 4 MA-6205-2023 his counsel.
However, no specific details or documentary evidence have been placed on record to substantiate the said explanation.
It is also noteworthy that the appellant was represented by counsel before the Claims Tribunal and was well aware of the proceedings.

The explanation furnished does not satisfactorily account for the entire period of delay nor does it Sonu Rawat vs Pradeep Kumar on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164033998/
2 disclose any compelling circumstance which prevented the appellant from approaching this Court within the prescribed period of 90 days provided under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

This Court is of the considered opinion that mere assertions regarding poverty, rustic background and lack of communication with counsel, without any supporting material, cannot constitute sufficient cause to condone such an inordinate delay.
9. In view of the aforesaid discussion, this Court finds that the appellant has failed to establish sufficient cause for condoning the delay of 244 days in filing the appeal.
10. Accordingly, I.A. No. 6865 of 2023 filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act seeking condonation of delay is dismissed.
Consequently, as the application for condonation of delay stands dismissed, the present Miscellaneous Appeal also stands dismissed as barred by limitation.
